NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, entirely dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and on HBM suppliers like SK Hynix and Micron for memory critical to GPU performance. Its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) and enterprise customers racing to build AI infrastructure, giving NVIDIA extraordinary pricing power but also concentration risk among a small number of very large buyers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the center of a vast global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless-like' designer that outsources manufacturing to a tightly managed network of specialized suppliers — most critically TSMC for silicon and Samsung/LG for displays — while distributing finished products through carriers, retailers, and its own direct channels worldwide. Its downstream relationships are uniquely bifurcated between hardware end consumers (via carriers and retailers) and platform ecosystem participants (developers, advertisers, and service partners) who collectively underpin Apple's high-margin Services segment.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the center of the global memory supply chain, depending heavily on a small number of specialized semiconductor equipment makers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its capital-intensive fab operations while selling DRAM, NAND, and HBM products to a diversified but concentrated set of hyperscalers, AI chip designers, and consumer electronics OEMs. Its strategic importance has surged with the AI infrastructure buildout, as HBM sales to NVIDIA and cloud customers like Amazon and Microsoft now represent a rapidly expanding share of revenue.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP supply chain, generating revenue through licensing its CPU/GPU/NPU architecture blueprints to virtually every major chip designer in the world rather than manufacturing silicon itself. Its upstream dependencies are primarily on EDA software vendors (Cadence, Synopsys) and cloud infrastructure, while its downstream relationships span the entire semiconductor ecosystem — from mobile giants like Apple and Qualcomm to hyperscalers like Amazon — making royalty revenue highly diversified but deeply tied to global chip shipment volumes.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at the intersection of fabless semiconductor design and data infrastructure deployment, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced-node wafer fabrication and ARM for processor IP while selling custom ASICs, networking silicon, and storage controllers to hyperscale cloud operators (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and networking/storage OEMs. The company has strategically pivoted toward high-margin custom silicon (ASIC) co-development with cloud titans, making hyperscaler capital spending cycles a primary demand driver for its revenue growth.
